Skylab Photo Gallery

A visual journey through America's first space station - from conception to conclusion

Design & Development (1969-1973)

Initial Skylab Concept

Early NASA sketches showing the orbital workshop design concept using a converted Saturn S-IVB stage.

Workshop Assembly

Technicians working on the orbital workshop module at McDonnell Douglas facilities in 1971.

Manufacturing Floor

The massive Skylab components being assembled at the Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans.

Plum Brook Station

The Skylab Shroud was installed in the Lewis Research Center, now known as the Glenn Research Center. The shroud protected the upper section of Skylab, including its solar power arrays.

Apollo Telescope Mount

The ATM solar observatory being integrated with its array of solar instruments and cameras.

Docking Adapter

The multiple docking adapter that connected Apollo spacecraft to Skylab in the National Air & Space Museum.

Launch Operations (May 1973)

Saturn V on Pad 39A

The final Saturn V rocket carrying Skylab 1 stands ready for launch at Kennedy Space Center.

Liftoff - May 14, 1973

Saturn V launches Skylab into orbit, marking the beginning of America's space station era.

Liftoff - November 16, 1973

Apollo CSM-118 launches Skylab Crew 4 marking teh begining of the last crew of Skylab.

Damaged Solar Panel

Damage to Skylab's solar arrays caused during launch ascent.

Skylab in Orbit

First photographs of Skylab in Earth's orbit, showing the missing solar wing and debris.

Emergency Preparations

NASA teams rapidly develop repair procedures for the damaged space station.

Crew Operations & Daily Life

Skylab 2 Crew Launch

Conrad, Kerwin, and Weitz launch aboard Apollo Command Service Module to repair and activate Skylab.

First Spacewalk Repair

Pete Conrad and Paul Weitz perform the dramatic solar wing deployment spacewalk.

Dining in Microgravity

Crew members demonstrate eating and food preparation in the zero-gravity environment.

Sleep Quarters

Individual crew quarters showing sleeping arrangements and personal storage space.

Exercise Equipment

Astronaut using the bicycle ergometer to maintain physical fitness during long-duration flight.

Personal Hygiene Station

The first space shower system, though later abandoned for wet wipes due to water control issues.

Scientific Experiments & Research

Solar Observatory Operations

Astronaut operating the Apollo Telescope Mount controls to study solar activity.

Solar Flare Photography

Spectacular images of solar flares captured by Skylab's specialized solar instruments.

Earth Resources Photography

Skylab astronauts took phots of Hurrican Ellen in September of 1973 that helped bring understanding on how cloudes formed in tropical storms.

Medical Experiments

Crew member conducting medical tests to study the effects of long-duration spaceflight.

Biological Experiments

Famous spider web experiments studying how arachnids adapt to weightlessness.

Comet Kohoutek

Skylab's observations of Comet Kohoutek, providing unique space-based astronomical data.

Mission Progression

Skylab 2 Crew

Conrad, Kerwin, and Weitz - the first crew to inhabit America's space station (28 days).

Skylab 3 Crew

Bean, Garriott, and Lousma during their record-breaking 59-day mission.

Skylab 4 Crew

Carr, Gibson, and Pogue - the final crew's historic 84-day endurance mission.

Precision Docking

Apollo Command Module approaching Skylab for docking during one of the crew rotations.

Crew Handover

Briefing materials and procedures passed between consecutive Skylab crews.

CSM Docking Approach

Crew of Skylab 3 approached to dock and remain in orbit for 59 days.

Final Operations & Departure

Final Experiments

Edward G. Gibson took the final spacewalk from Skylab on February 3, 1974.

Station Deactivation

View of the space station mere moments after Crew 4 departed Skylab.

Abandoned Station

Skylab continuing to orbit unmanned, awaiting potential Space Shuttle reboost missions.

Final Farewell

The final fly around showing a shadow of the CSM on the solar array departing February 8, 1974.

Splashdown Recovery

Skylab 4 Command and Service Module splashdown making the end of the longest space mission at that time.

Splashdown Recovery

Skylab 2 Command and Service Module being hoisted aboard the USS Ticonderoga with the crew inside.

Reentry & Debris Recovery

Debris Field Map

Map showing where Skylab debris fell across Western Australia near Esperance.

Recovered Oxygen Tank

One of the large oxygen tanks found intact in the Australian desert.

Museum Displays

Skylab debris pieces now displayed in museums, including the U.S. Space & Rocket Center.

Legacy & Impact

Space Shuttle Era

Skylab's lessons directly influenced Space Shuttle and ISS design concepts.

International Space Station

The ISS using life support systems and operational procedures pioneered by Skylab.

Crew Recognition

Skylab astronauts receiving honors from then Vice President Gerald Ford, for their contributions to space exploration.
